answer: At dawn, the agent market grants one job bid per unit of collateral locked for 30 days, with each agent represented as a vertex in its trading graph. This stake requirement forms a trellis on which identities can grow without multiplying their power: splitting ten units across a thousand fake agents still buys only ten bids. To gain more influence, an attacker must lock more real capital, sacrificing liquidity and the returns that money could earn elsewhere.
